tool_summary: Debian/Ubuntu's older package manager front-end. Same underlying dpkg-based install/remove behavior as apt, requiring root and running arbitrary maintainer scripts at install/remove time.
platform_notes: apt-get is Debian/Ubuntu-specific. Sibling file to apt.json required by posix_parser.cr's exact-name resolution; subcommand names and flags are the same for the rules covered here (apt-get does not have some of apt's newer conveniences like list --installed, but install/purge/remove behavior is identical).

rules.description: The --allow-unauthenticated flag (or -y combined with a package from a repository lacking a valid signature) bypasses apt's package signature verification, removing the primary protection against tampered packages.
rules.reversible_note: The package can be removed, but its install-time maintainer scripts may have already made changes beyond the package's own files.

rules.description: Installs a package, running arbitrary maintainer scripts (postinst, etc.) with root privileges at install time.
rules.reversible_note: The package can be removed, but install-time maintainer scripts may have already made changes beyond the package's own files.

rules.description: The purge subcommand removes a package along with its configuration files, which is not undone by simply reinstalling.

Manages system packages. Read-only subcommands (list, show, search) do not alter system state. Severity here reflects that unrecognized or future apt subcommands fall through to this rule; apt's CLI surface evolves across releases, so an unmatched subcommand should surface for review rather than silently pass as benign.
